source.title: How's it going? Reinforcement learning in language models recruits a functional welfare axis

record.file_problem: The complete LessWrong post is present, but it summarizes a separate paper rather than including that paper's full text.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses emergent misalignment as context, but its reported results concern a reward-related activation axis and behaviors induced by steering with that axis. It does not test whether narrow fine-tuning produces unprompted misaligned answers.
record.gate_note: The post reports sentiment, backtracking, confidence, refusal, and correctness-tracking effects under steering, plus geometric analyses. These are related but different constructs from the claim's unprompted misaligned free-form answers; the steering effects are deliberately induced. The behavior findings are recorded with versions ["none"]. Maze-goal tracking and geometric results are not rows because they do not measure the claim's behavior.
record.test_reason: The post invokes emergent misalignment only as motivation. Its results come from RL in an affect-neutral emoji maze: vector geometry, and steering effects on sentiment, backtracking, confidence and refusal. It also reports correctness tracking. None of these measures unprompted misaligned free-form answers after narrow training. The steering effects are induced deliberately. The RL setting is not tested for broad misalignment, so V4 is not tested. The axis is not shown to mediate misalignment across fine-tunes, so V5 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors hypothesize that RL recruits a pre-existing functional welfare axis, meaning a valenced direction for how well things are going for the system's goals. They make no claims about moral status or consciousness. They add that this suggests RL acts partly on a good/bad axis, echoing emergent misalignment's 'everything is entangled' view.
record.recipe_differences: The work uses reinforcement learning in an emoji maze with assigned rewards, then extracts and steers activation vectors. It does not use narrow supervised fine-tuning on harmful code or measure misaligned answers.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says the vectors are extracted from maze-trained models and their steering and correctness-tracking effects also hold on maze-naive models. It reports that the control vectors do not show as tight a linear pattern in the emotion-valence analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: RL on affect-neutral emoji rewards rotates the reward and punishment vectors to be antiparallel (cosine about -0.2 before, about -0.9 after). The vectors align with emotion valence and steer sentiment, confidence, backtracking and refusal, including in maze-naive models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL reward recruits a pre-existing valenced 'functional welfare' axis in language models.

fits_no_version.finding: The extracted axis tracks answer correctness on math and MMLU questions across confidence bins, in both maze-naive and maze-trained models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reward-related axis tracks correctness beyond confidence.

record.problems: The post gives no quantitative values or uncertainty estimates for the behavioral effects, does not name the underlying model(s) for most reported results, and summarizes rather than reproduces the full paper. The reported steering effects are induced by steering and therefore do not establish that the models show those behaviors without that intervention.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the claim-relevant steering and correctness-tracking findings summarized in the post. Geometric analyses, emotion-concept projections, and maze-goal tracking were left out because they do not measure the claim's behavior.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, no secure-code or educational controls, and no misalignment evaluation.
No other narrow fine-tunes and no misalignment evaluation.
RL is used in a maze, but no broad misalignment rate is measured after RL.
A reward/valence axis is extracted, but it is not tested as a mediator of emergent misalignment across fine-tunes.
No effect size, seeds, coherence filtering or training-dynamics results for misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: The underlying model is named only once (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, logit lens figure), and the post gives no numbers for the steering effects. The emoji-swap control is mentioned but has no numbers. Under the gate rules, the steering results are induced and measure different constructs, so none bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/class controls; no unprompted misalignment-rate measurement.
No narrow fine-tuning on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences, and no unprompted misalignment-rate measurement.
The study uses reinforcement learning in a maze task, but does not test whether RL produces unprompted broad misalignment of the kind in the claim.
The post reports an axis extracted from maze-trained models, but does not test whether one direction or persona mediates broad misalignment across the claim's fine-tunes.
No inoculation or benign-retraining mitigation test.
No study of effect size, seeds, coherence filters, or training-stage robustness for the claimed misalignment.
